# Poker Math Preflop Workbook: PDF pages 81–88

Source: [GTO/Poker-Math-Preflop-Workbook.pdf](../../../../sources/pdf/GTO/Poker-Math-Preflop-Workbook.pdf) · SHA-256 `9d4baec8d76af9666c6284e4db2fc518de90cc8c999b45dd94c8fbd54eb3fa22`

## PDF page 81

[Open source PDF](../../../../sources/pdf/GTO/Poker-Math-Preflop-Workbook.pdf#page=81)

```text
                       TIGHT RANGES


Instead of just looking at a small subsection of starting hands, let’s see how
your hole cards block a range of hands.

Each page lists your hole cards and your opponent’s range, along with each
combo from that range in a table below. Your job is to fill the table with the
correct number of combos for each starting hand after factoring in the
blocking effect (if any) of your hole cards. Then, sum up all of the combos
and fill in the box at the bottom of the page.

Use the same process that you did in the last section and either count the
combos by hand, or use software and manually put each of their starting
hands into the matrix.

This exercise gives you extra reps tying together combos and blockers. Pay
special attention to the blocking effect of Ax hands when your opponent has
hands like AA and AK in their preflop range.

For extra credit, note the percentage of the range your hole cards block com-
pared to having zero blockers at all. It is information like this that can help
you feel more confident bluff 3betting and less fearful that your opponent
always has a monster hand.

GLGL.




                                    PA G E 8 1
```

## PDF page 86

[Open source PDF](../../../../sources/pdf/GTO/Poker-Math-Preflop-Workbook.pdf#page=86)

```text
                      WIDER RANGES


Now you will see how your hole cards block a wider range of hands, this time
reusing the starting hand types from Chapter Four.

Each page gives your hole cards, your opponent’s range, and a table to com-
plete below. Add in the combos for each bucket, first ignoring your hole cards
(left column) and then factoring in your hole cards (right column).




Once you complete the table, add up all of the combos and fill in the box at
the bottom.

Pay special attention to how certain hole cards reduce specific buckets.
Where are Ax hands having the largest blocking effect, and where are T9s
hands having the largest blocking effect?

GLGL.


                                   PA G E 8 6
```
